title: I Have Loved You
backstory: Malachi speaks about a hundred years after the exiles came home from Babylon. The temple has been rebuilt and the offerings have started again, but the people's hearts have gone cold and they wonder aloud whether God still cares. God answers first with love, then with a question about the tired gifts they lay on his altar.

passages.synopsis: God's word comes to Israel through the prophet Malachi. The very first thing God says is, "I have loved you." The people answer back with a question: how have you loved us? God points them back to two brothers, Esau and Jacob, born into one family, and reminds them that it was Jacob he chose and loved, while Esau's land of Edom was laid waste and would not stand again however often it said it would rebuild. His love for them is older than their doubt, and their own eyes will yet see the LORD magnified from the border of Israel.

God puts a searching question to the priests, and names what is wrong with them: they are priests who despise his name. A son honours his father and a servant his master, so where is the honour due to God? They were bringing blind, lame, and sick animals to the altar, gifts they would be ashamed to hand their own governor, and calling the LORD's table contemptible. Not one of them, God says, would shut the doors or kindle a fire on his altar for nothing, yet they brought him what cost them nothing, and he takes no pleasure in offerings like that.

God looks past the tired temple to a wider horizon. From sunrise to sunset his name will be great among the nations, and a pure offering will be brought in every place. Meanwhile his own people call his table a weariness and bring what they do not want. God reminds them that he is a great King, and his name is worth their best.

God recalls his covenant with Levi, the family of the priests. It was a covenant of life and peace, and Levi's answer was reverence: the law of truth was in his mouth, and he turned many away from wrong. Priests were meant to be messengers, keeping knowledge on their lips so people could find God's way. Malachi's priests had wandered from that path, and their carelessness had led others astray.

triviaQuestions.question: What are the first words God speaks through Malachi?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Malachi 1:2 — "I have loved you, saith the LORD. Yet ye say, Wherein hast thou loved us? Was not Esau Jacob’s brother? saith the LORD: yet I loved Jacob,"

triviaQuestions.question: What kind of animals were the priests bringing to the altar?
options: The blind, the lame, and the sick
triviaQuestions.explanation: Malachi 1:8 — "And if ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil? offer it now unto thy governor; will he be pleased with thee, or accept thy person? saith the LORD of hosts."

triviaQuestions.question: Who carried this word of the LORD to Israel?
triviaQuestions.explanation: Malachi 1:1 — "The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi."

triviaQuestions.question: What did God say would happen to his name among the nations?
options: It would stay in Jerusalem only
It would be great among the Gentiles
triviaQuestions.explanation: Malachi 1:11 — "For from the rising of the sun even unto the going down of the same my name shall be great among the Gentiles; and in every place incense shall be offered unto my name, and a pure offering: for my name shall be great among the heathen, saith the LORD of hosts."

scrambleVerses.text: The burden of the word of the LORD to Israel by Malachi.
The LORD will be magnified from the border of Israel.
And ye shall know that I have sent this commandment unto you,

reflection: God begins by telling a tired people that he loves them. What would change in your worship if you truly believed that first?
